summary: This bill reorganizes the Department of Veterans Affairs' acquisition structure by establishing an Assistant Secretary for Acquisition, creating an Office of Acquisition, appointing Program Executive Officers and major acquisition program managers, and establishing a Director of Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation to oversee and improve the efficiency of major acquisition programs.

scores.thoughts: This bill focuses entirely on reforming the acquisition processes and cost assessment within the Department of Veterans Affairs. While the VA serves veterans, its operations are distinct from active military and defense spending. The bill does not allocate funds for military operations or defense programs, nor does it directly impact the budget of the Department of Defense, except for a minor provision allowing VA acquisition personnel to be certified by the DoD.

The bill is solely concerned with the internal organization and acquisition processes of the Department of Veterans Affairs in the United States. It has no provisions related to international aid, foreign assistance, or any spending outside of domestic veterans' services.
